11: # AI Runway AKS Setup
12: 
13: This skill walks users from a bare Kubernetes cluster to a running AI model deployment. Follow each step in sequence unless the user provides `skip-to-step N` to resume from a specific phase.
14: 
15: > **Cost awareness:** GPU node pools incur significant compute charges (A100-80GB can cost $3–5+/hr). Confirm the user understands cost implications before provisioning GPU resources.

17: ## Prerequisites
18: 
19: This skill assumes an AKS cluster already exists. If the user does not have a cluster, hand off to the `azure-kubernetes` skill first to provision one (with a GPU node pool unless CPU-only inference is acceptable), then return here.

33: - Set up AI Runway on an existing AKS cluster from scratch
34: - Install the AI Runway controller and CRDs

5: ## GPU Profiles
6: 
7: | GPU Model | VRAM (GB) | bfloat16 | float16 | Attention Backends | Compute Capability | Notes |
8: |-----------|-----------|----------|---------|-------------------|-------------------|-------|
9: | T4 | 16 | No | Yes | XFORMERS | 7.5 | No bfloat16 — must use float16 or float32. |
10: | V100 (16 GB) | 16 | No | Yes | XFORMERS | 7.0 | Limited flash attention. Prefer xformers. |
11: | V100 (32 GB) | 32 | No | Yes | XFORMERS | 7.0 | Same dtype constraints as 16 GB variant. |
12: | A10 | 24 | Yes | Yes | FLASH_ATTN, XFORMERS | 8.6 | Single-slot Ampere GPU. |
13: | A10G | 24 | Yes | Yes | FLASH_ATTN, XFORMERS | 8.6 | Good general-purpose GPU. Common in AWS. |
14: | L4 | 24 | Yes | Yes | FLASH_ATTN, XFORMERS | 8.9 | Inference-optimized. Common in GCP and Azure. |
15: | L40S | 48 | Yes | Yes | FLASH_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN, XFORMERS | 8.9 | Ada Lovelace. Growing availability on Azure. |
16: | A100 (40 GB) | 40 | Yes | Yes | FLASH_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN, XFORMERS | 8.0 | High-performance training and inference. |
17: | A100 (80 GB) | 80 | Yes | Yes | FLASH_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN, XFORMERS | 8.0 | Recommended for large models (70B+). |
18: | H100 | 80 | Yes | Yes | FLASH_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN, XFORMERS | 9.0 | Highest single-GPU performance. |
19: | H200 (SXM) | 141 | Yes | Yes | FLASH_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN, XFORMERS | 9.0 | Maximum memory (HBM3e). |
20: | H20 | 96 | Yes | Yes | FLASH_ATTN, TRITON_ATTN, XFORMERS | 9.0 | China-market H100 derivative. 96 GB HBM3. |
21: 
22: ### Attention Backends
23: 
24: | Backend | Description | Min Compute Capability |
25: |---------|-------------|----------------------|
26: | FLASH_ATTN | FlashAttention-2 — fastest, lowest memory | 8.0 (Ampere+) |
27: | TRITON_ATTN | Triton-based attention — good performance | 8.0 (Ampere+) |
28: | XFORMERS | Memory-efficient attention — works on older GPUs | 7.0 (Volta+) |

30: ## Compatibility Warnings
31: 
32: Surface these warnings when the following GPUs are detected:
33: 
34: ### T4
35: > **Warning:** T4 GPUs do not support bfloat16. You must configure `--dtype float16` in serving arguments. Failure to do so causes errors or silent dtype casting.
36: 
37: ### V100
38: > **Warning:** V100 GPUs do not support bfloat16 and have limited flash attention support. Use xformers backend and `--dtype float16`.

3: ## VRAM Sizing Guide
4: 
5: Estimate how much VRAM a model requires. Values are **weights only** — add 20–30% overhead for KV cache and activations during inference.
6: 
7: | Parameters | float16 / bfloat16 | int8 | int4 / GGUF Q4 |
8: |-----------|-------------------|------|----------------|
9: | 1B | ~2 GB | ~1 GB | ~0.5 GB |
10: | 3B | ~6 GB | ~3 GB | ~1.5 GB |
11: | 7–8B | ~14–16 GB | ~7–8 GB | ~3.5–4 GB |
12: | 13B | ~26 GB | ~13 GB | ~6.5 GB |
13: | 34B | ~68 GB | ~34 GB | ~17 GB |
14: | 70B | ~140 GB | ~70 GB | ~35 GB |
15: 
16: **Example:** 4× A100 80 GB = 320 GB total. Llama-3.1-70B at bfloat16 ≈ 168 GB with overhead — fits across 4 GPUs with tensor parallelism.
17: 
18: ## Starter Model Recommendations
19: 
20: | Cluster Capacity | Model | Provider | Notes |
21: |-----------------|-------|----------|-------|
22: | CPU-only | `google/gemma-3-1b-it-qat-q8_0-gguf` | KAITO (llama.cpp) | GGUF Q8; runs on CPU |
23: | 1× T4 (16 GB) | `microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct` | KAITO (vLLM) | ~8 GB float16; fits with headroom |
24: | 1× A10G/L4 (24 GB) | `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` | KAITO (vLLM) | ~16 GB bfloat16; gated — needs HF token |
25: | 1× A100 40 GB | `microsoft/Phi-3-medium-128k-instruct` | KAITO (vLLM) | ~28 GB float16; non-gated; MIT license |
26: | 1× A100 80 GB / H100 | `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` | KAITO (vLLM) | Oversized; upgrade to 70B if more GPUs available |
27: | 4× A100 80 GB | `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct` | KAITO (vLLM, TP) | ~168 GB; tensor parallelism; gated |

23: ## Gated Models (HuggingFace Token)
24: 
25: Llama-family models are gated on HuggingFace and require an access token. Read the token interactively to avoid exposing it in shell history:
26: 
27: ```bash
28: # Read token without echo, store in a securely permissioned temp file
29: hf_token_file="$(mktemp)"
30: trap 'rm -f "$hf_token_file"' EXIT
31: 
32: read -r -s -p "Enter HuggingFace token: " hf_token
33: printf '\n'
34: printf '%s' "$hf_token" > "$hf_token_file"
35: chmod 600 "$hf_token_file"
36: unset hf_token
37: 
38: kubectl create secret generic hf-token \
39:   --from-file=token="$hf_token_file" \
40:   -n <namespace> \
41:   --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
42: ```
